newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit sentiment stays weak, seen rangebound.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit sentiment stays weak, seen rangebound.

text.p: * Ringgit stayed weak on dollar bids by offshore players
* Dollar's rise expected to be capped at 2.5250 on fears of central bank intervention and local corporate selling
The ringgit remained weak against the dollar in early Asian trading, pressured by persistent dollar bids by offshore players, dealers said.

"The market is still short (of the dollar) and dollar/ringgit should be trading a little bit higher," said a European bank dealer in Singapore. "But topside is again expected to be capped at 2.5240/50."
He said dollar/ringgit remained well supported at the 2.5200 level with buying interest seen from offshore centres as well as Kuala Lumpur.
Dealers said corporate demand for the mid-year book closing has been one of the key factors contributing to the dollar's strength.
But dollar gains had been capped by fears of central bank intervention, dealers said.
Although there was no sign of Bank Negara's presence, dealers believed the central bank was monitoring the situation.
Dealers said there has been talk of stops above the 2.5250 level but the market appeared reluctant to test the resistance at 2.5250.
At 0230 GMT, the ringgit was quoted at 2.5223/28 a dollar. It closed at 2.5207/17 in Kuala Lumpur on Thursday.
